summary:
[  edit  ]
The DMX Out  CHOP  sends channels to  DMX ,  Art-Net ,  sACN ,  KiNET , or FTDI devices. Channel values for DMX are 0-255.
The first channel you send into the DMX Out will correspond to the first DMX address (DMX channel) As you add channels to the DMX Out, you will access the next DMX channels in order. For example, if you input 12 channels into the DMX out, you will be controlling DMX channels 1 thru 12.
The DMX in TouchDesigner was developed on the  ENTTEC  device, namely their  DMX USB Pro  and DMX over Ethernet devices, but it should work for many devices and software that support DMX/Art-Net/sACN/KiNET.
A Routing Table can be provided in a  DAT  where addresses can be specified by adding rows for each channel and specifying net, subnet and universe.
ENTTEC NOTE:  - Use ENTTEC's  NMU (Node Management Utility)  to configure and inspect the ENTTEC devices found on your network.
macOS NOTE:  - ENTTEC USB Pro may not connect automatically, to enable it enter the following command in the Terminal:
sudo kextunload -b com.apple.driver.AppleUSBFTDI
Tip : See the  OP Snippets  for setup and usage examples.
Tip : Use  WireShark  to watch your DMX network traffic.
See also:  DMX Out POP ,  Art-Net ,  sACN ,  DMX In CHOP ,  DMX

parameters.label: Active
parameters.name: active
parameters.description: Connects to the device while On.

parameters.label: Interface
parameters.name: interface
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select the type of interface to connect to the device with.

parameters.label: Enttec Generic Serial
parameters.name: serial
parameters.description: Uses the operating system's serial calls to write data.

parameters.label: Art-Net
parameters.name: artnet
parameters.description: Sets the interface to  Art-Net  protocol.

parameters.label: sACN
parameters.name: sacn
parameters.description: Sets the interface to  sACN  protocol.

parameters.label: KiNET
parameters.name: kinet
parameters.description: Sets the interface to  KiNET  protocol.

parameters.label: Format
parameters.name: format
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select between sending Packet Per Sample or Packet Per  Channel .

parameters.label: Packet Per  Sample
parameters.name: packetpersample
parameters.description: Each channel acts as a DMX channel, ie. 512 channels for 1 universe.

parameters.label: Packet Per  Channel
parameters.name: packetperchan
parameters.description: Each sample in a channel acts as a DMX channel. This allows for setting up a channel for each universe, ie. 1 channel with 512 samples for 1 universe. Add multiple channels for multiple universes.

parameters.label: Rate
parameters.name: rate
parameters.description: How often data is sent to the device (per second).

parameters.label: Serial Port
parameters.name: serialport
parameters.description: ⊞  - When the Interface parameter is set to Generic Serial this parameter lets you select which Serial (COM) port to use.

parameters.label: DMXking Port
parameters.name: dmxkingport
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select a DMXking port to send to.

parameters.label: Device
parameters.name: device
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select a DMX device from the menu.

parameters.label: Net (0-127)
parameters.name: net
parameters.description: When the Interface parameter is set to Art-Net, this sets the net address. A net is a groups of 16 consecutive subnets or 256 consecutive universes. The range for this parameter is 0-127. This is  not  a network IP address.

parameters.label: Subnet (0-15)
parameters.name: subnet
parameters.description: When the Interface parameter is set to Art-Net, this sets the subnet address. A subnet is a group of 16 consecutive universes. The range for this parameter is 0-15. This is  not  a network subnet mask.

parameters.label: Universe
parameters.name: universe
parameters.description: When the Interface parameter is set to Art-Net, this sets the universe address. A single DMX512 frame of 512 channels is referred to as a universe. The range for this parameter is 0-15.

parameters.label: Multicast
parameters.name: multicast
parameters.description: Enable multicast for sACN. Multicast automatically builds the IP based on Net, Subnet, and Universe of the device. This allows for sending to multiple devices at once by specifying multiple universes.

parameters.label: Network Address
parameters.name: netaddress
parameters.description: Specify the IP address to use. This address corresponds to the receiving device address.  When the address is set to its default 255.255.255.255, the messages are instead broadcast to all devices on the  network. The Art-Net Net, Subnet and Universe of the receiving devices must still match those specified in the DMX Out  CHOP  in all cases.

parameters.label: Local Address
parameters.name: localaddress
parameters.description: ⊞  - When the sending machine is equipped with multiple network adapters, this parameter can be used to choose which adapter to send the data from by specifying its IP address here.

parameters.label: Local Port
parameters.name: localport
parameters.description: In rare cases it can be necessary to supply a custom port from which the data should be sent. The default of  -1  means the O/S assigned port is being used.

parameters.label: Use Custom Port
parameters.name: customport
parameters.description: Enable the Network Port parameter to specify the port of the receiving hardware.

parameters.label: Network Port
parameters.name: netport
parameters.description: Let's you specify the port of the receiving hardware. By default and the spec of ArtNet this is set to 6454 and should only be changed in rare cases.

parameters.label: Send ArtSync
parameters.name: sendartsync
parameters.description: When enabled will send out ArtSync packets. ArtSync packets are used to synchronize multiple universes together. It will do this by waiting for all ArtDmx packets to finish sending, then follow up by sending an ArtSync packet.

parameters.label: ArtSync Timeout
parameters.name: artsynctimeout
parameters.description: Specify the time in milliseconds that ArtSync will wait for all ArtDmx packets to complete sending, before sending the ArtSync packet. If they have not all been sent when the timeout is reached, then ArtSync will terminate and the ArtSync packet will not be sent. Additionally, a new frame of ArtDmx packets will be sent and a new ArtSync will be initiated.

parameters.label: CID
parameters.name: cid
parameters.description: The unique ID of the sender.

parameters.label: Source
parameters.name: source
parameters.description: User assigned name of source (for informative purposes).

parameters.label: Priority
parameters.name: priority
parameters.description: The priority of the data being sent, if there are multiple sources.

parameters.label: KiNET Version
parameters.name: kinetversion
parameters.description: ⊞  - Set the version of the KiNET protocol to use.

parameters.label: Use Custom KiNET Port
parameters.name: customkinetport
parameters.description: When enabled, can specify a custom port for the KiNET v2 interface. When disabled, the port will be the broadcast port: 255.

parameters.label: KiNET Port
parameters.name: kinetport
parameters.description: Specifies the port for KiNET v2 interface.

parameters.label: Routing Table
parameters.name: routingtable
parameters.description: Available when using Packet Per Channel Format for Art-Net or sACN. Use the docked  Table DAT  to route channels to the appropriate universes. Addresses can be specified by adding rows for each channel and specifying net, subnet, universe, and netaddress. The net, subnet, universe, and netaddress columns are optional and correspond to the DMX Out  CHOP 's Net, Subnet, Universe, and Network Address parameters respectively. If for example the  net  column is missing from the Routing Table, the  Net  parameter is used instead.

parameters.label: Time Slice
parameters.name: timeslice
parameters.description: Turning this on forces the channels to be " Time Sliced ".  A  Time Slice  is the time between the last cook frame and the current cook frame.

parameters.label: Scope
parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: To determine which channels get affected, some CHOPs use a  Scope  string on the Common page. See  Pattern Matching .

parameters.label: Sample Rate  Match
parameters.name: srselect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Handle cases where multiple input CHOPs' sample rates are different. When Resampling occurs, the curves are interpolated according to the Interpolation Method Option, or "Linear" if the Interpolate Options are not available.

parameters.label: Resample At First Input's Rate
parameters.name: first
parameters.description: Use rate of first input to resample others.

parameters.label: Resample At Maximum Rate
parameters.name: max
parameters.description: Resample to the highest sample rate.

parameters.label: Resample At Minimum Rate
parameters.name: min
parameters.description: Resample to the lowest sample rate.

parameters.label: Error If Rates Differ
parameters.name: err
parameters.description: Doesn't accept conflicting sample rates.

parameters.label: Export  Method
parameters.name: exportmethod
parameters.description: ⊞  - This will determine how to connect the  CHOP  channel to the parameter. Refer to the  Export  article for more information.

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Index
parameters.name: datindex
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the index of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Name
parameters.name: datname
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the name of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: Channel Name is  Path : Parameter

parameters.description: The channel is the full destination of where to export to, such has  geo1/transform1:tx .

parameters.label: Export   Root

parameters.description: This path points to the root node where all of the paths that exporting by  Channel Name is  Path : Parameter   are relative to.

parameters.label: Export  Table

DMX Fixture POP * **¿Qué hace?** Este operador se utiliza para **construir "universos" DMX** a partir de una entrada POP, y se usa junto con un DMX Out POP para enviar señales DMX a dispositivos de iluminación u otros equipos. * **Características clave:** * Cada **primitiva** en la entrada POP es tratada como un **dispositivo (fixture)** DMX independiente. * El **perfil DMX** (qué canales DMX se usan para qué) se define en la página `Channels`. * Puedes usar atributos de primitiva especiales (como `DMXFixtureNet`, `DMXFixtureUniverse`) para personalizar la configuración DMX de cada dispositivo sin usar una tabla de enru
